skill.name: deploying-postgres-k8s
skill.description: Guides deployment of PostgreSQL on Kubernetes with the CloudNativePG operator. Covers operator installation, cluster manifests, secrets, backups, monitoring, troubleshooting, and cleanup.
skill.summary: Deploy CloudNativePG PostgreSQL clusters on Kubernetes with high availability, backups, and operational checks.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline command examples, and documented CloudNativePG installation URLs. The audit confirms plaintext PostgreSQL URI examples as high-risk copy-paste patterns and adds semantic findings for placeholder credentials and destructive PVC cleanup. No prompt injection evidence was found in SKILL.md or scripts/verify.py.

remediation.issue: Hardcoded database connection strings appear in example manifests and migration commands.
remediation.suggestion: Replace literal passwords with Kubernetes Secret references and show commands that read credentials from scoped secrets or local environment files.

remediation.issue: Copyable SQL and psql examples use placeholder passwords that may be reused unchanged.
remediation.suggestion: Use generated secrets in examples and add explicit instructions to rotate credentials before production use.

remediation.issue: Cleanup commands can delete persistent volumes and remove database data.
remediation.suggestion: Require namespace and context verification before destructive commands, and separate data-deleting steps from routine cleanup.

content.value_statement: Running PostgreSQL on Kubernetes requires operator, storage, secrets, backups, and operational checks. This skill guides CloudNativePG installation, cluster configuration, connections, backups, monitoring, and cleanup.
actual_capabilities: Installs the CloudNativePG operator with kubectl manifests or Helm charts.
Provides development, production, and bootstrap PostgreSQL cluster examples.
Explains CloudNativePG connection secrets and Kubernetes service endpoints.
Shows database access, migration workflows, and basic psql operations.
Covers S3 backups, scheduled backups, monitoring checks, troubleshooting, and cleanup.
limitations: It assumes an existing Kubernetes cluster with kubectl access.
It does not configure managed database services such as RDS, Cloud SQL, or Neon.
Examples require adaptation for storage classes, namespaces, secrets, and cloud credentials.
It does not validate production compliance, encryption policy, or disaster recovery objectives.

use_cases.title: Create a local database cluster
use_cases.description: Set up a small CloudNativePG cluster for development or integration testing on Kubernetes.

use_cases.title: Plan a production PostgreSQL deployment
use_cases.description: Design a highly available PostgreSQL cluster with resources, anti-affinity, monitoring, and backups.

use_cases.title: Operate Kubernetes database workflows
use_cases.description: Find commands for connection secrets, migrations, logs, status checks, backups, and cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Start a development cluster
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a non-production namespace.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me deploy a single-instance PostgreSQL development cluster on Kubernetes using CloudNativePG. Include prerequisites, commands, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create production manifests
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a CloudNativePG production PostgreSQL plan with three instances, resource settings, storage, anti-affinity, monitoring, and secret handling.

prompt_templates.title: Add backups and recovery checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through adding S3 backups and scheduled backups to a CloudNativePG cluster. Include validation checks and security notes.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot a failing cluster
prompt_templates.prompt: Help diagnose a CloudNativePG cluster that is not ready. Ask for relevant kubectl outputs, then propose likely causes and safe remediation steps.

output_examples.input: I need a local PostgreSQL cluster for testing.
output: Prerequisite checklist for Kubernetes access and CloudNativePG installation.
A development cluster plan with one instance, small storage, and verification steps.
Connection guidance using generated Kubernetes secrets.
A high availability design with three instances, storage sizing, resource requests, and anti-affinity.
Backup and monitoring recommendations using CloudNativePG features.
Security notes for secrets, service endpoints, and credential handling.

output_examples.input: My CloudNativePG cluster is not ready.
output: A diagnostic sequence for cluster status, pods, logs, and storage issues.
Likely causes mapped to practical remediation steps.
Warnings before destructive cleanup or persistent volume deletion.

best_practices: Use Kubernetes Secrets for all database credentials and avoid literal passwords in manifests.
Verify namespace, context, storage class, and backup destination before applying manifests.
Test restore procedures and failover behavior before depending on the cluster in production.
anti_patterns: Do not copy placeholder passwords into real clusters or migration commands.
Do not delete PVCs unless data loss is intended and backups are verified.
Do not use these examples as a substitute for compliance, encryption, or recovery planning.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy managed PostgreSQL services?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on PostgreSQL running inside Kubernetes with the CloudNativePG operator.

faq.question: Which operator does the skill use?
faq.answer: It uses CloudNativePG and references version 1.28 or later in the examples.

faq.question: Can it help with high availability?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a three-instance production pattern with anti-affinity and monitoring settings.

faq.question: Does it cover backups?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes S3 object store backup configuration and scheduled backup examples.

faq.question: What tools are expected?
faq.answer: You need Kubernetes access, kubectl, and optionally Helm for chart-based installation.

faq.question: Is it safe to copy every command directly?
faq.answer: No. Replace placeholder credentials, confirm the Kubernetes context, and review destructive cleanup commands first.
